title: Cancer screening by age: what and when
what: These are checks that help find cancer early, when nothing bothers you yet. Which ones depend on your age and sex.
why: For all adults by age; earlier and more often if close relatives had cancer or there are other risk factors.
duration: a visit usually takes 15 to 30 minutes, the checks themselves are on different days, and results take 1 day to 2 weeks
tell_doctor: Whether your parents, brothers, or sisters had cancer, and at what age
Whether you smoke now or smoked before
Which checks you already had and when
Whether you have complaints: blood, weight loss, lumps, a long cough

prepare.title: What is usually checked
prepare.text: The cervix and breast in women, the bowel in everyone from a certain age, and the lungs in smokers. Your doctor will give the exact list for your age.

prepare.title: Preparation
prepare.text: Each check has its own preparation. Ask the clinic about each one.

prepare.title: Papers
prepare.text: Collect the results of past checks, which helps avoid repeats.

bring: Results of past mammograms, smears, and colonoscopies
steps: The doctor asks about your health and your relatives
Decides which checks you need for your age
You have the checks on the set days
The doctor reviews the results and tells you when to repeat
feel: The visit itself does not hurt
Some checks can be unpleasant, but they are short
after: If all is well, the next check is set after the time suited to your age
If something is found, you will be sent for more tests, and that is not yet a diagnosis
Write down the dates of your checks so you do not miss one

faq.q: Why get checked if nothing hurts?
faq.a: Early cancer often does not hurt. That is exactly when it is easier to treat.

faq.q: If my mother had cancer, do I need to start earlier?
faq.a: Often yes. Tell your doctor, who will make a plan for you.

reminders.text: Cancer screening visit tomorrow. Bring the results of past checks.
